title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter
synopsis: When a storm cuts her island off from the mainland, a young woman discovers her father has been keeping more than the light burning. A slow-building drama about inheritance, duty and the stories families tell to survive.

title: Carbon Tuesday
synopsis: A climate negotiator with nothing left to lose locks forty delegates in a room and refuses to let anyone leave until they sign. Tense, talky, and far funnier than it has any right to be.

title: Mothlight
synopsis: Something is drawing the village children into the woods at night, and only the new schoolteacher seems to notice. Folk horror with patience and a genuinely upsetting final twenty minutes.

title: Six Weeks in Margate
synopsis: Two strangers agree to fake a relationship for one summer to satisfy their respective families. Warm, scruffy and sharply written, with a terrible karaoke scene that redeems itself.

title: The Cartographer's Error
synopsis: A mapmaker's deliberate mistake, planted in 1890 to catch plagiarists, turns out to describe a real place. Part detective story, part slow unravelling of a family that profited from the lie.

title: Orbital Decay
synopsis: The last two technicians on a decommissioned station have nine days of air and one working escape pod. Hard science fiction that trusts its audience to do the arithmetic.

title: Pennywhistle
synopsis: An animated adventure about a mouse who can only play one note, and the orchestra that needs exactly that note. Gorgeous hand-drawn work and a score worth the ticket alone.

title: The Quiet Part
synopsis: A radio host who has spent thirty years listening to other people's confessions finally has one of her own. Builds slowly to a single unbroken twelve-minute take.

title: Hollow Point Road
synopsis: A getaway driver takes one last job and discovers the cargo is a witness she is supposed to deliver to the wrong people. Lean, fast and mercifully free of sequel setup.

title: Every Other Weekend
synopsis: A father and his eleven-year-old daughter navigate two years of alternating weekends, told entirely through the car journeys between houses. Quietly devastating and often very funny.
